issues.legal_issue: A public servant commits criminal misconduct by abusing official position to obtain a valuable thing or pecuniary advantage for another person.
material_facts: The public servant applied for a plot under a scheme limited to specified sectors and was allotted a plot in one of those sectors on an as-is-where-is basis.
Despite the scheme and allotment terms not permitting the requested changes, the allotment was converted twice, ultimately securing a plot in a developed sector.
The plot was converted from a guest-house use to residential use and allotted to the public servant at a substantially lower premium than the rate applicable to that sector.
The plot’s area and layout were repeatedly altered without reasonable justification, and additional area was allotted after the lease had been executed.
The public servant’s official position was used to facilitate the allotments and conversions, and the public servant thereby obtained a valuable property and pecuniary advantage.
issues.conclusion: The public servant abused his position to obtain a valuable thing and pecuniary advantage; the conviction for criminal misconduct was properly sustained.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 13(1)(d)(i)–(iii) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, each of the three alternatives is independent and disjunctive: obtaining a valuable thing or pecuniary advantage by corrupt or illegal means, by abusing public office, or for another person without public interest is sufficient. Section 13(2) provides the punishment. The Court also applied the principle in Noida Entrepreneurs Association v. NOIDA, (2011) 6 SCC 508, that public power is held in trust and must be exercised reasonably, in good faith, and for the purpose for which it was conferred.

rule.if: public_servant_corruption_case and official_position_abused and valuable_advantage_obtained and (allocation_rules_bypassed or preferential_pricing or unjustified_property_alterations)

predicates.public_servant_corruption_case: The proceeding concerns an allegation that a public servant obtained a valuable thing or pecuniary advantage through the exercise of public office.
predicates.official_position_abused: The public servant used official authority or influence to facilitate a benefit for himself or another person.
predicates.valuable_advantage_obtained: The public servant or another person obtained valuable property or a pecuniary benefit.
predicates.allocation_rules_bypassed: The benefit was provided through allotments or conversions that did not comply with the applicable scheme or rules.
predicates.preferential_pricing: The property was obtained at a price materially below the rate applied to comparable property in its location.
predicates.unjustified_property_alterations: The property’s use, area, or layout was altered without a reasonable justification in a way that benefited the recipient.

issues.definition: When a public servant uses official position to obtain a valuable advantage and the benefit is connected with rule-bypassing, preferential pricing, or unjustified property alterations, criminal misconduct is established.

issues.legal_issue: A criminal conspiracy to secure an unlawful property benefit may be proved by inferring agreement and prior concert from the participants’ coordinated conduct and surrounding circumstances.
material_facts: One public servant sought and received successive conversions and allotments that departed from the applicable rules.
The other public servant, who headed the authority, approved key steps, including conversion of the plot’s use, its allotment, and the grant of additional area.
Records concerning the plot and its layout were altered, and the allotments were processed with unusual haste.
The resulting allotment gave one participant a valuable property and a substantial pecuniary advantage.
The participants’ actions were connected at multiple stages, although direct evidence of an express agreement was not produced.
issues.conclusion: The surrounding circumstances and coordinated acts established the appellants’ prior concert and supported their convictions for criminal conspiracy.
issues.legal_principle: Section 120-B IPC requires an agreement between two or more persons to do, or cause to be done, an illegal act or an act that is not illegal in itself by illegal means. Direct evidence of a conspiracy is often difficult to obtain, so its existence and object may be inferred from surrounding circumstances and the accused persons’ conduct. The Court relied on Yash Pal Mittal v. State of Punjab, (1977) 4 SCC 540; Ajay Aggarwal v. Union of India, (1993) 3 SCC 609; State of Maharashtra v. Som Nath Thapa, (1996) 4 SCC 659; and Ram Narain Popli v. Central Bureau of Investigation, (2003) 3 SCC 641. Knowledge of the unlawful act or unlawful means is necessary, and where the ultimate offence consists of a chain of actions, it is not necessary to prove that each conspirator knew every step the collaborator would take.

rule.if: public_servant_conspiracy_case and coordinated_official_actions and unlawful_property_benefit and (records_manipulated or undue_haste or repeated_rule_deviations)

predicates.public_servant_conspiracy_case: The proceeding concerns an alleged agreement between public servants to secure a property benefit through unlawful conduct or unlawful means.
predicates.coordinated_official_actions: Two or more participants took connected actions at different stages that facilitated the same benefit.
predicates.unlawful_property_benefit: The coordinated conduct resulted in a valuable property or pecuniary advantage being obtained through unlawful means.
predicates.records_manipulated: Records relating to the property or its allocation were deliberately altered or concealed.
predicates.undue_haste: The relevant authority processed connected requests unusually quickly without an adequate explanation for the urgency.
predicates.repeated_rule_deviations: The participants repeatedly departed from applicable rules in carrying out the connected actions.

issues.definition: When public servants take coordinated official actions that secure an unlawful property benefit, and the circumstances include record manipulation, undue haste, or repeated rule departures, criminal conspiracy is established.

issues.legal_issue: A custodial sentence may be reduced in light of the circumstances of the case, including the passage of time, surrender of the benefit, and the consequences of conviction for the offenders’ service and retirement benefits.
material_facts: The conduct occurred many years before the appeals were decided.
The public servant offered to surrender the allotted plot and forgo any refund.
The conviction placed the public servants’ employment and retirement benefits in jeopardy.
The appellants had begun serving their sentences.
issues.conclusion: The convictions were confirmed, but the custodial sentences imposed on both appellants were reduced; the appeals were allowed only to that extent.
issues.legal_principle: The Court considered the circumstances of the case when determining the custodial sentences, including the substantial passage of time since the occurrence, the offer to surrender the property without seeking a refund, and the consequences of conviction for the appellants’ service and retirement benefits.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_against_sentence and substantial_time_elapsed and benefit_surrendered_or_offered and service_or_retirement_consequences

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_sentence: The proceeding is a criminal appeal challenging a conviction or sentence that includes imprisonment.
predicates.substantial_time_elapsed: A substantial period passed between the conduct and the appellate decision.
predicates.benefit_surrendered_or_offered: The recipient surrendered, or offered to surrender, the benefit obtained through the conduct.
predicates.service_or_retirement_consequences: The conviction placed the offenders’ employment or retirement benefits in jeopardy.

issues.definition: In a criminal appeal, where substantial time has passed, the benefit has been surrendered or offered for surrender, and the conviction jeopardizes service or retirement benefits, the custodial sentence is reduced.
